headline.en: Bully in the Alley: hear the whole song first, then the tune on its own.

detail.en: The whole song, every part together
The guide sings it, line by line
Stop if anything tightens or hurts

headline.en: Now the tune on its own.

detail.en: Follow the words as it plays

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
Cecil Sharp took this chantey down from John Short of Watchet, and wrote that he had no other version of it and knew of no printed one.

source.en: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (London and Taunton, 1914), note to No. 35, p. 71, read from the scan

text.en: Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 3, then sing it back.
Hear line 4, then sing it back.
Now lines 3 and 4 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 5, then sing it back.
Hear line 6, then sing it back.
Line 7 is the tune of line 4 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Now lines 5 to 7 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 8, then sing it back.
Hear line 9, then sing it back.
Now lines 8 and 9 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 10, then sing it back.
Line 11 is line 6 again. Sing it with the guide.
Line 12 is the tune of line 4 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Line 13 is line 8 again. Sing it with the guide.
Now lines 10 to 13 joined, with the guide.
Line 14 is line 9 again. Sing it with the guide.
Line 15 is the tune of line 5 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Line 16 is line 6 again. Sing it with the guide.
Line 17 is the tune of line 4 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Now lines 14 to 17 joined, with the guide.
Line 18 is line 8 again. Sing it with the guide.
Hear line 19, then sing it back.
Now lines 18 and 19 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Refrain start to end, with the guide.
Verse 1 start to end, with the guide.
Verse 2 start to end, with the guide.
Verse 3 start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of Bully in the Alley in Sing, with the other parts playing.
It is a pulling chantey: Sharp marks with arrow-heads the notes the crew pulled on, here two in each chorus, on "Way" and on the "bully" right after it.

source.en: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (1914), p. 32 (the note on arrow-heads) and pp. 40 and 41, read from the scan
